title: Circuit Design Informed Adaptive Variational Quantum Algorithms
abstract: Resource-efficient computation is of central importance in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era, where decoherence, gate errors, and restricted qubit connectivity severely limit the reliable execution of quantum algorithms. In this work, we demonstrate that incorporating circuit design considerations is crucial for developing resource-efficient variational quantum algorithms. By focusing on the Hadamard test circuit architecture, hardware-aware qubit connectivity, and problem-specific adaptive framework, we analyze how circuit design constraints can systematically reduce the measurement overhead associated with repeated evaluations of the candidate gate pool in adaptive algorithms. Specifically, we demonstrate reductions in the required measurement resources ranging from at least 25% to as high as 50% - 55%. To assess the effectiveness of our approach, we investigate the ground state problem of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation. Overall, our work contributes to resource-friendly strategies for quantum computation and underscores that algorithmic frameworks should systematically integrate circuit design constraints with hardware-aware and problem-specific structures to enhance the practical feasibility of quantum devices in the NISQ era.
summary: This paper tackles the challenge of building efficient quantum algorithms for NISQ devices by integrating circuit design principles into adaptive VQA frameworks. By constraining the selection of candidate gates using structures like the Hadamard Test, the authors significantly reduce measurement overheads. This demonstrates a crucial pathway toward making variational quantum simulations more feasible on near-term hardware.
main_problem: Developing resource-efficient variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) suitable for the Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) era by systematically incorporating circuit design constraints.
main_result: Incorporating structural constraints, such as those derived from the Hadamard Test circuit, can reduce measurement overhead in adaptive VQA frameworks by 25% to over 55%.
method: The authors employ an adaptive framework that iteratively constructs variational ansätze while pruning the candidate gate pool using hardware-aware and problem-specific constraints.
model_or_system: The work is benchmarked on approximating the ground state of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLSE) Hamiltonian, which involves discretizing the spatial domain via finite differences.
key_observables: State infidelity ($F'$), measurement overhead/required measurement resources, and the size of the candidate gate pool ($\mathcal{O}_{	ext{pool}}$).
important_parameters: Nonlinearity strength ($g$), system size ($n$ qubits), and convergence indicators like $\epsilon_k$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that incorporating circuit design constraints systematically reduces measurement overhead, although the authors note that layered ansätze may not always be optimal.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate Hadamard test circuits, comparisons of gate pool scaling (showing pruning), and state infidelity ($F'$) vs. number of gates for both constrained adaptive methods and fixed layered ansatzes.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the resource limitations of NISQ devices, proposes an adaptive VQA framework incorporating circuit design constraints (like HT structure) to manage measurement overhead, benchmarks this approach on the NLSE ground state problem, and compares its performance against less constrained or fixed-layer ansätze.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses practical hardware limitations in quantum computation by providing algorithmic techniques that systematically reduce resource requirements for variational methods applied to physical models like the NLSE.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
